reviews.comment: Tries to be a down-to-earth prof, but he is not approachable and is rude whenever someone asks a bad question or a question he does not like. He grades harshly on tests and will not provide you with any additional resources to study for the test. Try to take any other prof as it may save your grade.

It felt like the course was not structured in a way that helped students succeed. A lot of things were unclear, the lectures were hard to follow, and there was not much guidance when it came to understanding the material. The class environment also felt pretty discouraging, so overall it was just a frustrating experience.

Professor HATES answering questions. I could not ask him a question without him sighing or looking frustrated. Always gives problems on exams that we have never seen before or done any examples of. Worst professor I have ever had, do not even bother going to office hours because he will not be helpful.

Was not very open to answering questions, if you asked anything, wanted to ignore you. Gave lectures only in person, online version posted does not match the stuff from class. The material is also a lot more conceptual than needed. Overall, a bad experience and bad teacher.

Dr. Elliott is one of best and most caring professors I've had. He is very accessible outside of class, and has fantastic lectures that make sense. He takes time out of lecture to ensure that students understand the content, and his homeworks and recitations properly ensure that students are prepared to apply concepts for exams and future classes.

He is always cracking jokes during lectures and tries his best to add some (much-needed) levity to a quite math and physics-heavy course. Whenever I needed to correct a test, he was very open to talking with me and generous with the points he gave back. Overall, a very funny and kind, would reccomend.

The thing I appreciate most abt Prof Elliott is he always goes big picture. He shows why problems matter in the career world, how topics fit in the curriculum, and how to be the best career engineer.  Homework is light. Tests are easier than hws. Super chill guy. Submitting hw late, missing class, or any issues is not a problem if you talk to him.

Amazing, caring, and hilarious prof! His whiteboard notes make lectures easy to follow and understand. HWs are tough & very lonl. Exam 1 & 2 fair but final much harder. Double-Sided Cheat sheet allowed. Quizzes are easy take-home. Great teaching—don't skip! Only downside: notes are hard to read if you miss class. Highly recommend!

Amazing professor and great lecturer! Attend class and you'll be well-prepared. Homework is tough but manageable with lectures. Two easy projects (15%) help boost your grade. Exams are fair and based on what he teaches. Clear explanations. Only downside is limited practice material for Exam 2 and the final. Still, one of the best to take!
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Elliott's lectures are very informative and can prepare you well for the class. Some quiz questions or homework problems can be a bit unfair, but he is helpful in office hours. He does have to be strict sometimes on grading, but overall tests are graded pretty leniently.

Elliott is a G. Dynamics/Vibrations is a tough class but you can tell he cares about the subject and cares about his students. Homework is tough but he is readily available by email and in office hours to answer questions. The notes he posts aren't great but you'll be fine as long as you attend class.

Elliott didn't know thermo too well. All he did was work examples directly from the book which he probably couldn't have been able to do himself without its help. However, tests were super easy and the group projects were basically a free 100 each (along with the fact that he curved BIG for 1st test). Overall didn't learn much but super easy class.
